Learn how we analyze your records

We start with the records you choose: phone use and your 1–10 mood ratings. We summarize what happened, compare days or sessions with enough data, and show a trend only when the records support one. Missing data is left missing, rather than treated as zero. A pattern is a clue to notice, not proof that phone use caused a mood change.
PhoneMood combines your phone-use records and mood ratings to look for patterns that repeat for you.
1. How long you used your phone
We summarize active phone time by day: your daily average, your usual range, and days that were clearly higher or lower. These numbers describe recorded use only; they do not infer your mood.
2. How use and mood may relate

We compare mood after lower and higher phone use in the 30 minutes before each check-in, accounting for the previous mood score, time between check-ins, and time of day. Incomplete usage windows are left out. The difference comes from your own long-term trends.
We look at overall phone use and individual apps alongside mood. For each app, we account for other app use, starting mood, and time of day, comparing scores at similar levels of total phone use.
4. Why results use points of mood

We express differences in use as an average difference in mood points. Overall phone use compares your lower and higher usage levels; app observations compare how you divide similar total usage time. We show up to three supported observations.

Early observations are patterns we can estimate from your records; they may change as more records arrive. We also leave out one day at a time to check whether the direction changes. When usage is too similar or records are incomplete, we keep collecting before showing an estimate.

The recent overview follows your date selection. Long-term observations build on your history independently of that selection. New records add information about your habits and mood, so observations may change over time.
JSON file with usage records, mood ratings and analysis results.
Mood analysis requires at least 20 valid ratings, plus enough sessions and comparable variation. Reaching 20 ratings does not guarantee a result. Existing records can still be exported.
Usage trends require at least 3 completed days with full records. Older records without completeness information are retained but excluded from the trend.
New installs default to 15 minutes of active use.
Keep checking in. As comparable records build up, observations about your phone use, apps, and mood will appear here.
